My work

Making technology approachable.

At the Hive, I help community members build the skills and confidence to use technology. My work combines hardware and software instruction, structured learning activities, and the day-to-day operation of the center's 3D printers. I adapt technical explanations to each visitor's starting point so they can understand the tools and use them independently.

Visitors instructed weekly
300+
Platforms covered by my curriculum
9

Responsibilities & Contributions

Hardware & Software Instruction

Teach hardware and software fundamentals to visitors across age groups and experience levels, from older adults learning everyday device skills to students exploring their first 3D models. Break technical tasks into approachable steps and help learners work through questions at their own pace.

Curriculum Development

Develop and deliver structured curriculum across nine platforms, including Swift, Tinkercad, and Sphero Edu. Organize hands-on activities that connect an explanation to a task learners can complete, practice, and build on.

3D Printer Operation & Maintenance

Operate and maintain the Hive's Flashforge 3D printers. Troubleshoot hardware failures, prepare print jobs, and adjust settings in Orca Slicer to improve consistency. Support the connection between a learner's digital model and a physical printed part.

The Engineering Connection

This role gives me regular practice translating technical concepts into clear instructions. Troubleshooting printers builds the same habits I use in engineering projects: identify the problem, work through possible causes, adjust the process, and check the result. Teaching also makes me consider usability early, because a tool only helps when someone can understand and operate it.

Why This Work Matters to Me

I joined IDIA in January 2025, and it remains some of the most fulfilling work I do. Seeing someone gain confidence with a device or hold a part they helped create makes the purpose of the work tangible. It shapes the kind of engineer I want to become: someone who builds things people can access, understand, and rely on.

Where I work

About IDIA & the Hive

The Institute for Digital Inclusion Acceleration is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit that helps people access the internet, build digital skills, and use technology in daily life. Its work addresses access to devices and connectivity alongside the skills and support needed to use them.

Hives are community technology spaces with access to digital devices, individual guidance from Digital Navigators, and opportunities to explore tools such as 3D printers, robotics, and virtual reality. IDIA's Digital Navigator model emphasizes personalized learning and building confidence with technology.
